addMachine.title: Add Machine
addMachine.sub: Once that machine logs in to your account it runs your tasks: nothing to approve.
addMachine.terminal: Terminal · as the user you code as
addMachine.powershell: PowerShell · as the user you code as
addMachine.waiting: Waiting for it to log in…
addMachine.logIn: Open it once installed, choose Log In and turn off “One of your devices” (a machine only), with the server
addMachine.password: The command asks for your password on that machine: it never goes on the command line.

addDevice.title: Add Device
addDevice.sub: A new computer or phone logs in with your account and password: nothing to approve, no code to compare. Lost one? Sign it out in Settings › Account & Devices.
addDevice.open: Install and open Aide on the new device, and choose Log In
addDevice.waiting: Waiting for the new device to log in…

addProject.title: Add Project
addProject.sub: A project is a folder where agents can work. Once it’s added, choose in each agent’s access which projects it can use.
addProject.name: Project name
addProject.worktreeHint: Git repository: each task works on its own branch and worktree, leaving the files you’re editing alone.
addProject.inPlaceHint: Agents make changes right in this folder, as if you ran Claude Code here yourself; there is no separate branch or change history.

scope.allAgents: All coding agents (including ones installed later)
scope.needProject: Choose at least one project, or “All projects”.
scope.needAgent: Choose at least one coding agent, or “All coding agents”.

scopeSheet.goneTitle: This Access Is No Longer Here
scopeSheet.saved: “{{name}}” now works with the new settings
scopeSheet.sub: Saving lists what changes; once you confirm, “{{name}}” works by the new settings at once and the old ones stop.

wake.linkSub: {{agent}} has made a routine that only a webhook starts. Paste its URL and key: then, when a task it started finishes or another agent writes to it, Aide wakes it.
wake.webhookSub: In the Grok desktop app, open the routine the bot created. In its Webhook section, click “POST to” or “key” to copy.
wake.pasteNote: You can also paste both into either field. The key stays in Aide and is never shared with the bot.
wake.tryingSub: Aide is sending a test wake; the bot will also read any waiting messages.
wake.okSub: The test wake succeeded. From now on, Aide will wake the bot automatically whenever new messages arrive.
wake.okCost: Each wake triggers one bot run.
wake.secret: Signing secret, for custom webhooks that verify signatures (shown only once)
wake.manageSub: When new messages arrive, Aide calls this webhook.
wake.removeMessage: Aide will stop calling its webhook. Incoming messages will still be queued for it.
wake.reason400: Received HTTP 400: check if the routine is paused
wake.reasonURL: Received HTTP {{status}}: webhook not found, check the URL
wake.reasonBusy: Bot is busy (429): try again shortly

erase.title: Erase Everything in Aide?
erase.sub: Aide on all your devices will be reset to a clean install.
erase.devicesDesc: Signed out, with their task history and settings removed; one that is a machine too also loses its projects and worktrees
erase.machinesDesc: Signed out, with their projects, task history and the worktrees Aide made removed
erase.agentsDesc: Signed out; they log in again to come back
erase.serverDesc: The account and the server’s key are cleared: it is not set up any more, with a new setup code
erase.laterDevice: offline: will prompt to reset when next opened
erase.laterMachine: Offline: log it in again later
erase.laterAgent: must sign in again when next used
erase.stayProjects: Your project folders, git repositories, and branches
erase.stayWorktrees: Worktrees with uncommitted changes (moved aside and preserved, with their paths shown afterward)
erase.stayOffline: Data on offline devices until each device is reset
erase.confirm: This action cannot be undone. Type {{text}} to confirm:
erase.progressSub: Devices online are erased now; offline ones reset or log in again the next time they are used.
erase.stateDevice: Will prompt to reset when next opened
erase.stateAgent: Must sign in again when next used
erase.finishFailed: This Mac couldn’t finish erasing local data: {{error}}
erase.finishFailed_win: This PC couldn’t finish erasing local data: {{error}}

herOff.eraseDesc: Her’s assistants, conversations, memory, routines, files, connectors and model logins on “{{name}}” are deleted. This can’t be undone. Off, they stay, and Her carries on when you turn her on again.
herOff.offline: “{{name}}” is offline, so Her’s data stays on it.

newSession.title: New Task
newSession.sub: Start a coding agent on one of your machines. It shows as started by you, and you can keep sending it messages.
newSession.repoHint: {{machine}} clones it with its own git login; Aide stores no GitHub credentials. Nothing is pushed unless you ask.
newSession.noOffers: {{agent}} hasn’t told this machine its models or modes yet; they show after its first task here. Its own defaults apply.
newSession.promptPlaceholder: What should {{agent}} do? (!plan or !implement first; #s_… brings in an earlier session)
newSession.howToConnect: How to Connect DSH, Claude Desktop…

contacts.title: Contacts
contacts.sub: Pick a contact and write to it: the message goes on in the task it works in when that can take one, else a new task starts on its machine and project, with its settings.
contacts.none: No contacts yet. Add one: name it, pick its machine, project and agent.
contacts.fresh: The next message starts a new task with its settings.
contacts.name: Name
contacts.presetsNote: Changing the machine, project, agent, model, effort or mode starts a new task with the next message; a new name or avatar keeps the task. Deleting a contact keeps its tasks.
